Cash NAS100 is 29,124.46, down 297.09 points or 1.01%, inside a 29,038.22 to 29,250.41 range whose low is untested for a fifth cash hour. NQ futures are 29,153.00, down 1.00%. VIX has firmed to 17.93 from 17.73 an hour ago but still holds under its 18.05 high, the ten-year is 4.944% just below a 4.952% session high, the two-year is 4.569%, and Brent has eased to $107.49 from a $108.32 high. Mean reversion has continued to function through the afternoon, so tail stays in the low band.
recommendation: Tail at 17 maps the policy state to EA_ON for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD, with pause false and caution false under the fixed repository mapping. The danger window stays drawn narrowly around 12:30 to 14:00 UTC on 11 September, covering the August consumer price release, the first hour of post-release price discovery and the 13:30 UTC cash open. Oracle's results after today's close and the 21:00 UTC call are carried as scheduled checkpoints inside the forecast rather than grounds for widening the window, because Oracle is NYSE-listed and reaches the Nasdaq-100 only indirectly. Stress at 86 remains the elevated part of this assessment and does not by itself change the mapped state.
headline: Cash NAS100 29,124.46 and NQ 29,153.00 hold mid-band into the final cash hour with the 29,038.22 session low untested for a fifth hour; tail edges from 16 to 17 as VIX firms to 17.93, the ten-year holds 4.944% and Brent eases to $107.49 ahead of Oracle results after the bell.
body:
The hour changed the calendar position more than the structure. Cash NAS100 is 29,124.46, down 297.09 points or 1.01% on the day, and NQ futures are 29,153.00, down 1.00%. The 29,038.22 opening-auction low remains untested for a fifth cash hour, and the roughly 212-point band between it and the 29,250.41 high has now contained the entire session. Price has continued to trade in both directions inside that band, which is the observation that carries the most weight in this framework: tail measures the probability of a price path that denies meaningful mean reversion long enough to overwhelm a reverse or grid approach, not the size of the day's decline.

The cross-asset backdrop remains the difficult part. The ten-year yield is 4.944%, just under its 4.952% session high and the highest since 2023; the two-year is 4.569%, up about twelve basis points; the thirty-year has printed 5.36%, the highest since 2007. Brent has eased to $107.49 from a $108.32 high but is still up more than 6% on the day, with the move attributed to unresolved Gulf shipping disruption and no credible de-escalation path. VIX has firmed to 17.93 from 17.73 an hour ago while staying below its 18.05 session high. Semiconductors were the weak leg through the session and megacap participation was split, with Apple higher and Nvidia lower.

The macro anchor for the day was the August producer price report, which printed final demand up 0.4% on the month and 5.4% over twelve months, above expectations, and which has firmed pricing for a possible rate increase at the 16 September FOMC meeting. That is the mechanism behind the yield move and, through it, the pressure on index multiples. Under the framework used here, event importance and surprise magnitude raise stress and shape confidence; they raise tail only once an observed price path denies retracement. No such path has appeared today.

Two scheduled checkpoints sit inside the forward window. Oracle reports fiscal Q1 2027 results after today's close with a call at 21:00 UTC, into the thinnest futures liquidity of the cycle; the company is NYSE-listed, so the index transmission is a sentiment read-through on AI capex rather than a weight effect. The August consumer price release then prints at 12:30 UTC on 11 September, three trading days before the FOMC decision, and is the reason the danger window is drawn where it is. Neither checkpoint has produced an observed price path yet, so both are carried as conditional risk in the forecast rather than as current tail.

lookbackSummary: All 24 clock-hours from 19:00 UTC on 9 September to 18:00 UTC on 10 September carry a published Claude assessment, so every lookback slot is available and none is reconstructed. The window opens at tail 12 with a mixed read, troughs at 8 to 9 across the U.S. close and the first overnight hours, and holds a 9 to 11 band through the Asian and European morning. The regime change sits in the middle of the U.S. session: tail 14 at 11:00 UTC as the mode turned trend-down on the pre-release grind, 20 at 12:00 UTC when the producer price report printed and the mode became event/whipsaw, and a 24 peak at 13:00 UTC covering post-release discovery and the cash open. The last five slots record the decay back into range, 17 then 14, a 16 tick as yields and oil extended, 15, and 16 at 18:00 UTC. Stress never left the extreme band, running 80 to 86 throughout, which is the defining feature of this window: a difficult, high-volatility tape in which mean reversion nonetheless kept working.
outlookSummary: The forward window opens in the last full cash hour of 10 September and closes in the New York afternoon of 11 September. Conditional tail starts at 17, steps to 19 across the 20:00 and 21:00 UTC slots covering the cash close and Oracle's scheduled results and call into thin futures liquidity, then decays through 17 and 14 into the late evening. It settles to an 11 floor across the Asian hours, where no U.S. macro is scheduled, and rebuilds gradually from the European pre-market, 12 through 14, reaching 16 in the final hour before the release. The window peak is 23 in the 12:00 UTC slot that contains the August consumer price print and 22 in the 13:00 UTC slot where post-release discovery overlaps the cash open; both map to WATCH and neither reaches the block threshold, since no post-release price path is observed. The path then eases to 19 at the University of Michigan release, then 17, 15 and 14 for the final Friday slots. Stress stays in the extreme band throughout, peaking at 89 across the two release hours, and confidence declines from 88 to 70 with distance from observed evidence.
